ak_red_gate.blurb: Red Gate is a small roadside sport crag on the Seward Highway south of Anchorage, filed under the highway's rock cluster. It holds seven bolted lines, with a spread running from 5.8 up to a single 5.11, and most of the weight sitting around 5.8 to 5.10. The cliff is best known for slabby faces, and some of its pitches run longer than is typical along this corridor. Expect traffic noise right beside you. The corridor as a whole has a reputation for loose, chossy rock, so a helmet is wise. Recent roadwork is reported to have altered or removed parts of the wall, so look it over before committing to a route.

ak_shot_rock.blurb: Shot Rock is a short blasted roadcut right beside the Seward Highway south of Anchorage. Its seven climbs are mostly easy bolted lines in the 5.4 to 5.7 range, plus a trad line and a single easy boulder problem, which makes it a handy spot for a quick warm-up or for newer leaders. Holds are mostly old drill scars and other features left by blasting, and the rock is reported to be better than much of the corridor. The drawback is noise: you stand only a few feet from passing traffic. Wearing a helmet is sensible anywhere along this stretch of road.

ak_tsaina_river_gorge_wall.blurb: This is a small steep wall above the Tsaina River beside the Richardson Highway north of Valdez. Seven routes mix sport and trad, with two easier lines around 5.6 and 5.7 and most of the rest clustered near 5.10. Every route is reached by rappelling in from the top, so bring ropes and be ready to descend before you climb. The walk from the road to the rim is only a few minutes, yet the setting feels remote, and the wall is described as catching plenty of sun. The wider Valdez rock is a little chossy, so move carefully.

ak_sheep_creek_2.blurb: Sheep Creek is a drainage near the base of Thompson Pass, east of Keystone Canyon in the Valdez area, offering seven ice routes, many of them multi-pitch and up to roughly 800 feet tall. The grades skew hard: one WI3, one WI4, four WI5 lines and a single WI6. Two of the routes can be seen from the highway, while the rest are reached by hiking up the drainage. All of the lines sit under heavy avalanche exposure, so reading snow conditions matters here. This is a place for experienced ice climbers rather than first-timers.

ak_victor_creek.blurb: Victor Creek is a drainage on the Kenai Peninsula between Anchorage and Seward, grouped with the Lakes District ice climbing. It has six ice routes ranging from WI2 to WI5, most of them around WI4. Climbs near the road can be reached by walking up the frozen creek, while the bigger lines farther up the valley are reached by the established trail. The creek holds some chunky multi-pitch ice along with one of the more technical lines in the region, so it suits climbers who already have steady ice experience.

ak_hatchery_wall.blurb: Hatchery Wall is a winter crag on the shore of Trail Lake on the Kenai Peninsula, in the Lakes District. Six routes of about 25 to 45 metres cover a range from friendly easy ice to harder bolted mixed lines; the ice grades here sit at WI3 and WI4, with four of the six at the harder end. The walk in is short, roughly ten minutes from a nearby trailhead. More lines are still being developed, so expect fixed gear and projects that belong to the people establishing them.
